newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks down 4.47 pct as Wall St drops.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks down 4.47 pct as Wall St drops.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed down 4.47 percent on Monday as a big slide on Wall Street sent the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange reeling, traders said.
Buenos Aires -- which was closed last Thursday and Friday -- took a double-whammy from the New York Stock Exchange, which also fell in its last session before the Easter break.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV ended at 706.
Still, traders insisted local investors kept their nerve and were not panicked into big selling, with most of the downward momentum coming from slumping American Depositary Receipts.
The yield on the U.S. long bond, which has been luring money out of stocks, rose to 7.10 percent. Limp Argentine Bradies also depressed the Buenos Aires stock market.
"The day's saving grace was that there was no panic. The locals were not selling, and it was all just following the U.S, market," one trader said.
Turnover was a moderate $19.8 million. The general stock index slipped 3.36 percent, with two shares closing up, 45 down and four steady.
The MerVal closed down 0.7 percent Wednesday at 739.15, paring last week's holiday-shortened gains to 1.2 percent.
